rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. 1) An amended petition was filed, when the issues with the initial petition could have been addressed in a verified supplement. An amended pleading requires the same notice as the pleading it amends, including publication. [CRC 7.53(a).] The published notice was just for the initial petition, not the amended petition. The Court to determine if publication of notice of the amended petition may be waived. 2) The estate reportedly consists of just $983.00 in personal property and $12,000 "out of state land." No California court has jurisdiction over real property in another state. The (amended) petition does not appear to be necessary. Please have the CASE NUMBER and the CASE NAME ready for the clerk. Parties appearing must check in for the hearing using their FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear in person or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF MO'MIN ABDUN NOOR
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/28/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) The only correct form of notice for a petition for appointment of a personal representative is the mandatory Judicial Council form Notice of Petition to Administer Estate. (2) The proof of service (of the incorrect form of notice) filed on 8/17/26 (e-filed 8/18/26) is incompletely verified. Please provide a courtesy copy of the complete, verified proof of service of Notice of Petition to Administer Estate (with remote instructions attached and showing the 10/28/26 hearing date) to the assigned examiner by 10/14/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. (NB: A supplement should not AMEND a pleading. [See CRC 7.3 for definitions.] An amendment requires notice (including publication). [CRC 7.53(a).] A supplement does not ordinarily require additional notice. [Probate Code Sect. 1205 and CRC 7.53(b).] Issues raised by the court should be addressed in a supplement or amendment that stands on its own and simply provides the missing or correct information, not to clarify deficiencies, which are not otherwise part of the record. A missing proposed order should just be provided. Defective notice should just be cured by filing the proof of service of the correct notice. It is not necessary for a party or counsel to file a NOTICE OF REMOTE APPEARANCE (RA-010) before making a remote appearance. [LRSF 14.1 C.1.a.])
